blockers.summary: non-attested complete-verified accepts a forged validation result plus a forged work.validation.observed event in <git-common-dir>/praxis; attested mode (PRAXIS-REL-009) refuses it, and PRAXIS-REL-006's rollout gate requires requireAttestedEvidence with requireVerifiedCompletion
blockers.note: requireVerifiedCompletion now implies attested evidence unless allowUnattestedEvidence is set, and every completion is labelled attested or unattested. A repository that requires neither still accepts the non-attested GATE-3/C3b forgery, now recorded as unattested; this is inherent to non-attested mode and documented as not forgery-resistant.

blockers.status: resolved (scope: protected policy and pinned trust root)
findings: the attestation policy is read from the completing worktree ros.json
the authority path is caller-chosen, so an agent can pin its own key
blockers.note: The completion policy is read from the protected base, and attestation requires workProtocol.trustedVerifierKeyIds to pin the host verifier keyid. GATE-A5 (PROBE-3) is refused with POLICY_CHANGED and GATE-A6 (PROBE-4) with UNTRUSTED_AUTHORITY on v3.19.0; both completed as verified on v3.18.0. Remaining documented limit: a process that can rewrite refs/remotes/origin/HEAD, origin/main or the protected history controls the protected source too, so the host must still audit verifierKeyIds and the authority path after the fact.
blockers.breaking: Repositories that already require attested or verified completion must add workProtocol.trustedVerifierKeyIds (the host verifier keyid) on the protected branch before their next attested completion; until then it fails closed with PRX.COMPLETION.UNTRUSTED_AUTHORITY.
